title: lore read-only graph-cache generations block worktree removal fleet-wide (opum-ai/opum-fleet OFLE-339)
description:
Read-only modes on .lore/cache generations leave directories that an EXTERNAL recursive delete cannot remove. Measured fleet-wide by opum-desktop on 2026-10-15; filed against opum-fleet as OFLE-339 (the earlier rm -rf variant is OFLE-320).

REPRODUCTION. Run any lore query (or lore check) in a checkout, then delete the checkout recursively. The cache generation directory .lore/cache/graph/ladybug/<version>/generations/<key> is mode 0555, with index.json 0400 and projection.lbdb 0444 inside, so deleting its contents needs a write bit on the containing directory. git worktree remove deletes the worktree gitfile and then fails partway, leaving a directory with no .git that holds only the lore cache; opum-fleet repo-root guard then refuses to clean an unknown no-.git directory, which is correct.

ANSWER (measured in source at origin/dev ce57b688, 2026-10-19): the modes are DELIBERATE, not incidental. src/core/ladybug-lifecycle.ts:369 seals the database 0444 and :371 seals the generation directory 0555; :766 opens the control manifest 0400 (writeControlManifestLast). ADR docs/adr/0018-persistent-local-graph-projection-with-ladybugdb.md:62 states that generations are immutable and opened read-only. test/ladybug-lifecycle.test.ts:258-260 and :349-351 assert no write bit is set on the generation directory, the database, the control manifest and the published files. The lore removal path already thaws first: removeContained calls makeDirectoryTreeWritable (src/core/ladybug-lifecycle.ts:1003). The defect is therefore that immutability is enforced without an owner-facing way to delete the cache, not that the modes are wrong.

SCOPE: the operator decides through opum-doc between (a) a lore-side fix, for example a lore cache clear / lore clean command (or a lifecycle removal step) that thaws and deletes the tree, and (b) a guard carve-out allowing removal of a no-.git directory that contains only .lore/cache. This task records the defect and the answer only.

HELD: not to be worked before the 0.14.0 pair release lands.
implementationNotes:
DEC-208 (opum-doc tracker) decides LCLI-740 as a lore-side fix: a cache-clear command. It stays HELD until plan approval; do not start building. Relayed from the decision record on 2026-10-19.
Spec:
1. An owner-invoked command that clears a checkout's `.lore/cache`, reusing removeContained -> makeDirectoryTreeWritable.
2. It touches only the bundle's own cache and refuses any other path.
3. Prove it both ways: it removes a populated cache, including the 0555 generation directory, and it refuses a path outside `.lore/cache`.
4. ADR-0018 is unchanged, so the generations stay immutable while they live.
5. It ships in the next pair release after 0.14.0. It is a new item for the next DEC-205 plan approval. It is not on the DEC-182 floor unless it touches CI workflows, so the `sensitive` label comes off unless it does.

DEC-208 design note, producer survey (2026-10-19). A shell-less reviewer unit that never ran lore still left a read-only .lore cache in its worktree, so the clear must cover every producer, not only the CLI.
PRIMARY producer: the opum-lore pane mod, hooks/register.tsx. In plugin versions up to 0.13.0 its session.start handler auto-opened the pane, and its initial read-back and 30-second refresh ran two `lore` reads per tick in EVERY Claude process, teammate, headless and workflow units included; those reads build `.lore/cache`. LCLI-705 (9ab611c6, shipped in lore 0.14.0) gates session.start on `!e.isInteractive || $CLAUDECODE === "1"`, so from 0.14.0 those processes spawn zero lore children and register no clock. A unit running an older opum-lore is still ungated, which is how a unit that never ran lore leaves a cache behind.
OTHER producers are lore commands themselves: `lore query`, `lore check`, `lore sync` and `lore agent context` all build or refresh the graph. Two fleet-side callers reach them without a person typing lore: the opum-workflow PreToolUse hook sync-lore-after-tracker-write.sh runs `lore check` and, on failure, `lore sync` after a tracker write; and the assignment skills' prepare step runs `lore agent context <role>`.
Design consequence: the 'clear lore cache, then git worktree remove' order must not assume the unit ran a lore command itself, and must handle a cache produced by the pane mod, by the tracker-write hook, or by an assignment context pack.

DEC-208 design input, 2026-10-20 (relayed after the producer survey). The cache-clear must also work on a directory that is NO LONGER a registered worktree. A failed `git worktree remove` deletes the gitfile and then fails partway, stranding a directory with no `.git` that holds only the read-only `.lore/cache`; that directory is exactly the case a worktree-scoped command would refuse. One such directory exists today: a failed removal left `opum-marketplace/.claude/worktrees/review-ts25-1c08492` stranded with its read-only cache inside.
So the command must take a path the CALLER names and operate on `<path>/.lore/cache` whether or not git still knows that directory as a worktree, without requiring `git worktree list` membership as a precondition. It must still refuse any path that is not a `.lore/cache` under a path the caller names (DEC-208 item 2), so the widening is in what counts as a live checkout, not in what the command will delete.
Not to be built: held for the next plan.

REVIEW VERDICT for opum-ai/lore-cli#666 at 5b839e0f33f25f3d763a589f2aab78fdb0cb6a51, recorded VERBATIM from the unit transcript (SendMessage body, 9493 bytes, sha256 ec922bd71551e4d64e063c14445504b84983d510c3564c18e86a7e3a70734121). Unit lore-cli-review-666, model claude-opus-5-5 (read from its transcript), worktree .claude/worktrees/lore-cli-review-666. Follow-ups filed as LCLI-762.

VERDICT lore-cli#666 5b839e0f33f25f3d763a589f2aab78fdb0cb6a51: APPROVE

No BLOCKING findings. DEC-208 clause 1 is met: the command touches only <checkout>/.lore/cache, it reuses the lifecycle's own removeContained, and the tests prove both arms. Clause 3 holds: no repo-root or lore-cache carve-out was added, and `DEC-176` does not appear anywhere in src. Four LOW findings follow, and none of them is a containment escape that an ordinary single-actor run can reach.

FINDINGS

1. INFO, containment is sound. src/core/ladybug-lifecycle.ts:449-476. The real guard is three things together: realpath(<checkout>) (canonicalRepositoryRoot at :1077), then lstat refusing a symlinked or non-directory `.lore` and `cache` (:457-473), then deletion only of the fixed lexical join(root,".lore","cache"). Per input:
   - `..` and relative paths are normalised by resolve() before anything is derived.
   - A nonexistent path is not_found (exit 3).
   - A symlinked <path> is deliberately followed by realpath, so it clears the TARGET's real .lore/cache. That is the user's own naming, but it is worth knowing.
   - Handing it .lore/cache directly works lexically (:452-453). If .lore is a symlink in that case, it is still refused, because root is the parent, re-lstatted.
   - A path inside the cache (e.g. .lore/cache/graph) is treated as a checkout. That gives .../graph/.lore, which is `absent`, and nothing is removed.
   - Symlink entries INSIDE the cache are safe. makeDirectoryTreeWritable (:1047-1053) chmods only Dirents where isDirectory() is true and isSymbolicLink() is false, and a symlink Dirent reports isDirectory()=false, so chmod never goes through a link. rmSync then unlinks links rather than following them (Node semantics; see unverified item a).
   - Hard links: files are never chmodded and unlink removes only the name. Directories cannot be hard-linked.
   - Nothing outside the cache is ever chmodded on the non-racy path.

2. LOW, a TOCTOU window. ladybug-lifecycle.ts:473→475. If `.lore` is swapped for a symlink after the lstat loop and before removeContained, then lstat(cacheDir) in removeContained (:1038) resolves through the intermediate `.lore`. makeDirectoryTreeWritable then chmods 0700 outside, and rmSync recurses into outside/cache. A narrower window of the same kind exists for any subdirectory swapped for a link between readdir and chmodSync (:1049-1051), where chmod follows the link. Both need a concurrent same-user racer against an owner-invoked command. The existing lifecycle removal has the same shape, so this is not a regression. Non-blocking. If anyone wants it hardened, the fix is rename-then-delete or an fd-relative walk, and it belongs on LCLI-761-style hardening rather than in this PR.

3. LOW, assertContained is tautological here. ladybug-lifecycle.ts:474: `assertContained(root, cacheDir)`, where cacheDir = join(root,".lore","cache"), is always contained lexically, so it adds nothing. The docstring at :447 ("or one resolving outside the checkout, is refused") credits it with work the lstat loop actually does. The lstat refusal is also partly redundant, because `!isDirectory()` on an lstat'd symlink already refuses it. So dropping only `isSymbolicLink() ||` would redden no test. That is redundancy, not a defect.

4. LOW, the contract says 4 for a permission failure, but the code exits 1. docs/reference/cli-surface.md:726 documents "`4` ... or read/write denied", and src/core/manifest.ts:770 advertises [0,2,3,4] via the "read" seam. In the code:
   - The lstat loop rethrows any non-ENOENT errno raw (:463).
   - removeContained rethrows raw (:1042).
   - chmodSync and rmSync throw raw EACCES, EPERM or EBUSY, for example when .lore is not writable, a file carries a uchg flag, or a Windows DB handle is open.
   None of those is a LoreError, so exitCodeFor (src/errors.ts:279) returns 1 (EXIT_UNCAUGHT) and the error is reported as "uncaught". Either wrap those errors as denied or correct the doc and manifest line. Removal is arguably the "write" seam ([4,5]) rather than "read".

5. LOW, a cwd inconsistency that also makes the missing e2e test riskier than it looks. src/commands/cache.ts:20 ignores options.root, and clearCheckoutCache does resolve(pathInput) against process.cwd(). Sibling commands resolve user paths against root, e.g. validate.ts:125, explorer.ts:225, agent.ts:707. In production RunContext.cwd is only an injection seam with no CLI flag (src/cli.ts:83,686), so behaviour today is correct. But an in-process e2e test written the usual way, `run(["cache","clear","."], {cwd: tmp})`, would clear the TEST RUNNER's cwd, which is the lore-cli checkout's own .lore/cache. Suggest `resolve(options.root, positional)` in cache.ts before the call.

6. LOW, design question for opum-doc via the leader, not a code defect: L102 returns `absent` rather than refusing. Clause 1 says "refuses any path outside it" and requires proof that "it refuses a path outside .lore/cache". My reading is that <path> names a checkout, not a deletion target, and the deletion target is always derived as <path>/.lore/cache. So no path outside the cache can ever be the target, and "touches only" holds (L102 asserts docs/page.md and the real cache both survive). The proof-both-ways "refuses" arm is met by L82 and L92, which throw LoreError (denied, exit 4) for the realistic outside-pointing shapes.
   What is NOT delivered is a hard error, with a nonzero exit, for a directory that is not a checkout. There is also no bundle check at all: any directory with a real .lore/cache qualifies. The stranded-worktree case (no .git) needs that, and no user-global .lore/cache exists (no homedir() use in src). If opum-doc reads "refuses" as "a non-checkout <path> exits nonzero", that is a contract change for them to rule on. I agree with the writer that it is a design question, not something to fix unilaterally.

7. INFO, reuse is literally true (DEC-208 "reusing its existing make-writable-then-delete path"). clearCheckoutCache calls the same private removeContained (:1035) and makeDirectoryTreeWritable (:1047) that disposeLadybugProjection (:426), cleanupAbandonedStaging (:1027), the staging path (:348, :356) and generation pruning (:905) already use. There is no parallel implementation. It deliberately does not reuse disposeLadybugProjection, which needs ensureCacheLayout, the writer lock, and the ladybug sub-root rather than the whole .lore/cache. That fits the ruling. Taking no writer lock means a concurrent lore writer in the same checkout could see errors mid-build. This is documented (cli-surface.md:718-719) and acceptable for an owner action on stranded checkouts.

8. INFO, wrapper behaviour (src/commands/cache.ts):
   - The wrong verb or arity is usage, exit 2 (:17-18).
   - not_found is 3, via canonicalRepositoryRoot.
   - Symlink and non-directory refusals are denied, exit 4 (:466).
   - `cleared` and `absent` are both exit 0, with kind cache.result.
   - Text output is "cleared <path>" or "nothing to clear: <path> does not exist".
   This matches cli-contract.md:246, the cli-surface.md table (apart from finding 4), and test/help.test.ts:158/219 (exit codes [0,2,3,4], kind cache.result). The skills/lore/SKILL.md:92 line matches the manifest summary at manifest.ts:765.

9. LOW, test strength. The proof map checks out (L60, L69, L76 accept; L82, L92, L111 refuse; L102 absent). Two caveats:
   (a) The writer's mutant (removeContained → plain rmSync) reddening exactly L60 and L69 proves the THAW, not containment. Containment is pinned by the toThrow assertions in L82, L92 and L111. L82's "outside file survives" assertion passes even with no guard at all, because rmSync unlinks a final-component symlink, so only its toThrow discriminates. L92 (symlinked intermediate .lore) is the one case where a missing guard would really delete outside. That is the important test, and it is present.
   (b) No test covers a symlink entry INSIDE the cache pointing outside, and no test covers a subdirectory link. Add one: cache/link -> outside dir holding a 0555 subdir. Assert it clears, outside survives, and outside's mode is unchanged. That pins both rm-does-not-follow and chmod-does-not-follow.
   The missing end-to-end `lore cache clear` invocation test matters a little, not a lot. It is the only test that would catch findings 4 and 5. If one is added, it must pass an absolute path or fix finding 5 first.

NOT VERIFIABLE FROM A TREE READ
a. That Bun's rmSync({recursive:true}) unlinks symlinks rather than following them, at the top level and for nested entries. Node does; Bun's native rm is believed to, but I could not run it. L82 passing in CI is evidence for the top-level case only.
b. That removeContained and makeDirectoryTreeWritable are byte-unchanged from the parent 0c6934c4. I had no git diff. Their call sites elsewhere in the file show they pre-existed, and the "-1" is plausibly the node:path import line (:29, now carrying `sep`), but I could not confirm it.
c. The CI result (6 required contexts, 13 pass, 1 skipped) is taken from the brief. I had no gh.
d. How realpathSync handles case on macOS under Bun. It only affects which path is reported; with case-variant input, namesCache is false and the result is `absent`, so nothing is deleted.
e. I could not run `quest instructions overview` (CLAUDE.md asks for it on every request) because I have no shell. I made no tracker reads or writes beyond reading LCLI-740.json's presence.

No worktree was touched.
finalSummary: Landed in opum-ai/lore-cli#666 (CI run 39957561957 on head 5b839e0f; 13 pass, 1 skipped): lore cache clear <path> deletes a checkout's whole .lore/cache through the lifecycle's removeContained thaw-and-delete path, with no git, no writer lock, nothing created, symlinked or non-directory .lore/cache refused. Both-ways proof in test/cache-clear.test.ts; Opus review APPROVE recorded verbatim in the notes. Review follow-ups are LCLI-762 and must land before the next pair release. It ships in the next lore/quest pair release (DEC-208 clause 5), and the fleet worktree hold lifts when it ships, not now.
